en.text:
General situation: Over the past 30 days, global grains and oilseeds markets have remained stable with no significant bullish or bearish shifts. Bunge (BG) faces margin compression risks as soybean input prices rise faster than soy oil and meal outputs, compounded by high leverage post-Viterra merger and uncertain biofuel tax credits. Brazilian soybean exporters show reluctance to offer CFR China shipments due to freight and phytosanitary certification risks, despite strong crush margins and improving meal sales in China. Black Sea wheat prices have inflated by 5-7% month-on-month, supported by freight parity enabling exports to ASEAN countries. What changed vs previous comparable period: This 30-day window shows increased market activity compared to the prior month, which had no recorded reports. Price inflation in Black Sea wheat and cautious Brazilian export offers contrast with the prior quiet period. Actionable implications for trading/brokerage: Traders should monitor Bunge’s margin squeeze risk and debt profile before engaging. Brazilian soybean export offers may remain tight, potentially supporting prices. Black Sea wheat exports to ASEAN remain attractive due to freight parity, suggesting opportunities in that corridor. Freight market disruptions noted last week may further impact logistics costs and timing. 

Key facts:
- Bunge trades at 10x EV/EBITDA with $12.2B debt post-Viterra merger as of March 18, 2026.
- Black Sea wheat FOB prices inflated 5-7% vs prior month (March 12, 2026).
- Brazilian soybean offers to China limited due to freight and phytosanitary risks (March 11, 2026).
- INR/USD exchange rate steady at 93/94 supporting export competitiveness (March 12, 2026).
- Chicago USDA wheat prices remain above $600/MT, underpinning regional price support.
- Freight market disruptions and spikes reported late March may increase shipping costs and delays.
